page: Amazon Web Services x8g.metal-24xl is a bare-metal, memory-optimized server powered by 96 dedicated physical cores of the 64-bit ARM architecture. It utilizes the AWS Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz, featuring 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 1536.0 GB of DDR5 memory, providing a high resource density of 16.0 GB of RAM per core. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 40 Gbps, has no local storage, and does not include GPU accelerators.

Benchmark data reveals top-tier multi-core and memory performance. The server achieves top 10% placement in multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with cached read-only speeds reaching 11096.57 GB/sec and large-block uncached write speeds at 215.99 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is moderate, placing in the middle 50% for single-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Additionally, while LLM text generation for medium and large models is strong, text generation for small 135M models falls into the bottom 10%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the x8g.metal-24xl offers high resource density by combining 96 dedicated physical ARM cores with a massive 1.5 TB DDR5 memory footprint on a bare-metal platform. This profile is highly optimized for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of virtualization. It is best suited for large-scale database operations, in-memory caching systems like Redis, high-throughput web serving, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
